headline: Earnings jump on stronger fees and easing credit costs
summary_short: Diluted EPS of $1.23 was up 37% y/y and 13% q/q as fee income grew 5.9% q/q on equity-investment gains and the provision for credit losses fell 17.5% q/q to $395 million, while Truist returned $1.8 billion to shareholders via dividends and buybacks.
summary_long: Total revenue-TE rose 2.2% q/q to $5.31 billion as noninterest income grew 5.9% on higher income from equity investments, while NIM-TE slipped four basis points to 2.98% on higher funding costs. Noninterest expense rose 2.4% to $3.06 billion on higher variable incentives and continued technology investment. Credit quality held firm: the NCO ratio fell 11bp to 0.50% and provision for credit losses dropped 17.5% q/q to $395 million, though nonperforming loans ticked up to 0.51% of loans. CET1 rose 10bp to 10.9% on retained earnings and lower risk-weighted assets. Truist repurchased $1.2 billion of shares and declared a $0.52 dividend, a 121% total payout ratio; no numeric forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: CEO Bill Rogers attributed the quarter to "disciplined execution against our strategic priorities," citing higher fee income, strong credit performance, and capital returned to shareholders as EPS rose 37% y/y.
EPS growth outpaces net income growth because average diluted shares fell 5.1% y/y from continued buybacks, layered on higher revenue and a lower y/y provision for credit losses.
Tracks diluted EPS growth on the same net income increase and the 5.1% y/y decline in average shares outstanding from buybacks.
Release attributes the y/y improvement to higher investment banking, trading, and wealth management income and a lower provision for credit losses, partially offset by higher personnel expense.
Reflects continued share buybacks — $1.2 billion repurchased this quarter — consistent with the 5.1% y/y decline in average diluted shares outstanding.
